legend: MARS Dev Team Weekly Report — Legend & Run Notes
Report week: Monday 8/24/2026 – Friday 8/28/2026 (worklog export covers Mon 8/24 – Sun 8/30/2026)

Run type: WEEKLY run. This is NOT the final weekly run of August — per the plan set at the end of the Aug 17–23 run, one more short "Aug 31" period remains before month-end (Sun Aug 30 is the last day covered by this week's export; Monday 8/31 falls in a week that otherwise spans into September). Per the standing project rule, the [Month] Month-to-Date tab is SKIPPED this run — only Weekly Summary, Dev Closes, QA Closes, and the 5 Raw Log tabs are built.
Scope & exclusions
• Only the 53 people on the roster (Project Knowledge) are tracked. Not on roster, excluded from this week's worklog: Beez Khumin-taylor, Bricen Bennett.
• Not on roster, excluded from PTO processing: Beez Khumin-Taylor, Beth Bailey, Catherine Sanders, Jameka Blanchard, Katie Wiggins, Linda Jones, Tyler Higgins.
• Excluded ticket prefixes (customer-facing): PSC, PS, MSP. 26 distinct excluded ticket keys appeared in this week's worklog.
• Each person's "Total" row in the worklog export is excluded before summing, per spec (prevents ~2x double-counting).

• Batch-log rule (>12h on one ticket on one day, excluded from totals, flagged in Notes): no entries met this threshold this week. Allen McAfee logged exactly 12.0h on a single ticket on two separate days (TIN-423 Mon 8/24, TIN-434 Wed 8/26) — right at the boundary, but the rule is ">12h" (strictly greater), so these are NOT excluded.

• Implausible-daily-total check (many tickets, no single entry >12h): I flagged this internally using a >15h/day threshold (double the standard 7.5h workday) as a reasonable, but not spec-specified, bar for "worth verifying." No person's day exceeded this threshold this week, so nothing is flagged in Notes. Flag me if you'd rather use a different threshold.

• Data-quality exclusion: PNP-4715's two changelog rows are column-shifted in the source CSV export (an unescaped quote inside the issue-summary text broke the column alignment for this ticket only, the same failure mode as MAIN-7987 in an earlier run). Both affected rows show status "Backlog" (no transition), so excluding this ticket has zero effect on bounce/close attribution this run — flagged for completeness only.

• Katherine Theos logged 20 minutes on Saturday 8/29 (MAIN-9020) — outside the Weekly Summary's Mon–Fri daily columns, so it doesn't appear in a daily cell or in her Wk Total, but it is counted in her Tickets Worked (she is credited with having worked that ticket during the report week).
Numeric weekly targets used (per-person, from roster "Rough Hrs Per Week")

Developer/Jr Dev/QA/Other = 30, Data Engineer = 25, Senior Dev = 15–20 (17.5 numeric), Staff Engineer = 10–15 (12.5 numeric). Two Developers carry an individual range instead of the flat default: Rimon Berhe and Colin Knecht are both "20 to 30" → numeric 25, displayed "20-30". Senior Devs Halina Bobrykava and Aleisha DeYoung are "15 to 20" → 17.5, "15-20". Staff Engineer Erin Terre is "10 to 15" → 12.5, "10-15". Erin Terre and Halina Bobrykava are tracked normally in this run, same as everyone else on the roster.
PTO handling notes specific to this run
• Timecard export has no separate "Status" column, so every row is treated as already-approved, per spec.

• Two PTO/leave requests that started in the PRIOR week spilled a chunk into this report week once spread at 7.5h/day across weekdays: Alex Secor's 15h PTO request (started Fri 8/21) lands its second 7.5h chunk on Mon 8/24 (full PTO day); Amanda Esposito's 22.5h Bereavement request (started Thu 8/20) lands its third 7.5h chunk on Mon 8/24 (full PTO day, consistent with her showing 0 logged hours that day in the worklog). A third, Jared Rosenthal's 22.5h PTO (started Fri 8/28), spills the OPPOSITE direction — 2 of its 3 days land in the following week (Mon 8/31, Tue 9/1) and are outside this run's scope.

• Britt Heyward's 37.5h Unpaid-Time-Off request (started Sat 8/29) spreads entirely into 8/31–9/4 per the weekday-skip-weekend spreading rule, so it has zero effect on this report week; her separate 7.5h Unpaid-Time-Off request on Fri 8/28 IS a full PTO day within this week.

• Every non-"PTO"-labeled benefit type observed this week (Late In, Early Out, Sick (PTO), Bereavement, Unpaid Time Off) was treated as time away from work per spec, not just rows literally labeled "PTO".
Dev-owner attribution & bounce-back — judgment calls flagged this run

The full back-walk correction from the spec (walking back through a tight ≤60s, status-unchanged, assignee-only reassignment row when a hand-off/closure row's own assignee field is static) was applied throughout. Of 351 qualifying hand-off/direct-close events in the full history, 31 had the reassignment on the same row (the literal base case), 47 required and received the back-walk correction, and 273 had a static assignee with no qualifying tight predecessor (used as-is — a genuine, non-split assignment).
Two status-category judgment calls, because the source data contains a few status labels the spec doesn't explicitly enumerate:

1. "Testing" (generic) and "Offshore Testing" appear a handful of times in the full-history changelog but are not in the spec's literal 5-item Testing-status list. I classified both as Testing-equivalent (by clear name analogy) rather than falling back to the open-ended "dev-stage" catch-all — the alternative would have credited a "skip testing" close to a developer for a ticket (CL-1335) that visibly DID pass through a testing-named status. This affected a small number of tickets (CL-1316, CL-1335, CL-1337); only CL-1335 (JC Collins) had roster-crediting impact, and classifying it as testing-equivalent means it is NOT counted as a "skip" Dev Close for him.
2. "Select For Development" (a capitalization variant of "Selected for Development") is treated as the same status for the bounce-back Dev-status landing list.

3. "Closed" (distinct from "Done") appeared twice (CL-1324, CL-1355) — I did NOT treat it as equivalent to "Done," so neither ticket counts as a Dev Close. Both look like tickets closed without real dev work (straight from "To Do", one credited to a QA-role assignee), consistent with treating "Closed" as a different outcome (e.g. duplicate/won't-fix) rather than a completion. Flagging this in case the spec intends otherwise.

A related observation worth your attention rather than silent delivery: the Dev-owner attribution rule is not role-restricted, so a QA-role roster member can end up credited with a "Dev Close" if they were the assignee of record at a qualifying hand-off/closure event. This happened at real scale this run — Katherine Theos (QA) is credited with 22 MTD Dev Closes, more than any Developer on the roster, almost all CL-prefix tickets. Spot-checking a few: several (e.g. CL-1360, CL-1289) are clean — she was assignee from creation through an automation-driven close, no dev-stage detour. One (CL-1331) is murkier: the ticket ping-ponged between her and a developer (Jonathan Collins) through a "Review" status in the final minutes before Done, and "Review" isn't in the spec's Testing or Dev-landing lists, so it fell into the open dev-stage catch-all — meaning whoever happened to hold the ticket at the literal Review→Done transition got the credit. I'm not confident this individual case reflects genuine dev ownership, and I did not adjust the mechanical rule on my own judgment — flagging it here so you can decide whether "Review" should be added to a recognized list.
Weekly Summary column scoping

The "Dev Closes" column on Weekly Summary is WEEK-scoped (tickets reaching Done Mon 8/24–Sun 8/30), consistent with every other Weekly Summary metric being week-scoped. The separate "Dev Closes" and "QA Closes" TABS are Month-to-Date scoped, per spec, and list the underlying ticket keys.

This week's and this MTD's figures happen to be numerically IDENTICAL: every "Done" event found anywhere in the supplied Issue History CSV (which nominally spans back to Dec 2023) falls within this single report week. The pre-August rows in this export are extremely sparse (a few dozen scattered rows total, mostly single ticket-creation stubs for long-lived tickets) — 2,644 of 2,870 total rows are dated in August 2026 alone. I can't independently verify whether this reflects the team genuinely closing nothing earlier in August, or whether this export has thinner historical coverage than the one used for earlier August weekly reports (which discussed nonzero July/earlier-August figures). Worth reconciling against last week's numbers if this looks off. MTD total: 220 tickets reached Done in the Aug 1–30 window; 71 unattributed (no qualifying hand-off/skip event ever visible for that ticket — under-counted on purpose per spec, rather than mis-crediting a guess); 38 credited to a real but non-roster person (QA/PM/other team members such as Katie Wiggins, Bricen Bennett, Beez Khumin-Taylor, or in one case a Jira automation account that was literally the assignee of record) and so not counted toward anyone on this roster.
QA Closes limitation

Only 13 worklog entries this week matched the "PARENT-KEY: PARENT-KEY | QA" sub-ticket pattern, all logged by Nherissa Dagal. Of their 13 distinct parent tickets, 2 (MAIN-9151, MAIN-9013) reached Done within the Aug 1–30 MTD window — these are the only QA Closes credited this run. Because QA Closes depends on WORKLOG data (not the full-history changelog), and only this week's worklog export was supplied for this run, any parent ticket that reached Done earlier in August with its QA sub-ticket time logged in an earlier week's worklog (not available here) would be missed. This is in addition to the standing limitation that QA time logged directly on a parent ticket (no sub-ticket) is never captured.
Formatting & formula notes

Arial 10 throughout. Daily cells: PTO green fill with literal "PTO" display (underlying value 0, so SUM formulas correctly treat it as no contribution); partial-PTO days show the logged number with a trailing "*" via number format (underlying value is the real logged hours, so it still sums correctly) with a matching Notes entry; RED/ORANGE/OK shading on non-PTO days compares that day's logged hours to that day's (PTO-adjusted) goal. Wk Total is a real =SUM() formula over the five daily cells. Low Hours Flag is a real IF() formula comparing the Wk Total and Prorated Wk Target cells in the same row. Tickets Worked, Bounced, Bounce Rate %, Bounce Flag, Low Volume Flag, and Dev Closes are script-computed values — they depend on the changelog state-machine (dev-owner back-walk, bounce exclusions) and set-union logic (worked ∪ bounced) that can't be expressed as plain same-row spreadsheet formulas, per the spec's documented exception for this. Recalculated with the xlsx skill's recalc.py; 0 formula errors confirmed before delivery.

qaCloses.note: Limitation: only captures QA testing logged on a dedicated 'PARENT-KEY | QA' sub-ticket whose parent reached Done in the MTD window; QA time logged directly on the parent ticket (no sub-ticket) is not captured. Additionally, this run's MTD figures reflect only the sub-ticket logging visible in THIS WEEK's worklog export -- prior weeks' worklog files were not re-supplied for this run, so a parent ticket that closed earlier in August with QA sub-ticket time logged in an earlier week would not be captured here.
